title: Choco-Q: Commute Hamiltonian-based QAOA for Constrained Binary Optimization
problem: Existing QAOA approaches for constrained binary optimization based on penalty terms or cyclic Hamiltonian simulation fail to encode arbitrary linear constraints, yielding near-zero success rates (as low as 0.02%) and long end-to-end latency. Decomposing the resulting Hamiltonians into deployable quantum circuits has exponential time and memory complexity.
motivation: Constrained binary optimization (NP-hard problems such as facility location, scheduling, and graph coloring) is a target workload for quantum advantage, but the extremely low success rates of current QAOA designs eliminate any practical quantum benefit.
method: Choco-Q encodes constraints directly into the quantum algorithm by selecting a driver Hamiltonian that commutes (stays mathematically compatible) with the constraint structure, which guarantees that quantum solutions always satisfy all requirements—achieving 100% success. To make this runnable on today's quantum hardware, it applies three optimizations: breaking the constraint structure into independent pieces reduces circuit depth from approximately 4,000 to 24 operations; converting these to basic quantum gates (control-phase and CX gates) takes linear time instead of exponential time, replacing an otherwise expensive standard method; removing variables with redundant solution entries further shrinks qubit count and circuit depth. The approach is tested on IBM quantum processors—Fez (159 qubits), Sherbrooke, and Osaka (127 qubits)—and on an A100 GPU simulator.
key_novelty: The core idea is using the commute Hamiltonian as the driver for QAOA (Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm), which universally encodes any linear constraint exactly and decomposes into deployable circuits in linear time.
contributions: First QAOA framework achieving 100% in-constraints rate for arbitrary linear equality constraints via commute Hamiltonian encoding

Hamiltonian serialization technique that decomposes the global commute Hamiltonian into local sub-Hamiltonians with provably preserved constraint satisfaction, reducing circuit depth from thousands to tens
Exact linear-complexity decomposition of local commute Hamiltonians into control-phase and CX gates, eliminating exponential Trotter approximation overhead (10^6x decomposition time reduction)

Variable elimination technique for further circuit depth reduction on NISQ devices; overall 235x algorithmic improvement in success rate and 4.69x end-to-end speedup over cyclic Hamiltonian-based QAOA

metrics.speedup: 4.69x end-to-end over cyclic Hamiltonian-based QAOA on real IBMQ hardware
metrics.accuracy: 235x improvement in success rate; 100% in-constraints rate; 658x improvement in approximation ratio gap vs. cyclic Hamiltonian
metrics.other: 10^6x decomposition time reduction; circuit depth reduction from ~10^4 to ~100; 2.65x in-constraints rate improvement on IBMQ

limitations: Circuit depth still grows linearly with problem size and number of constraints, limiting scalability to problems well within current NISQ qubit counts (tested up to 28 variables).
primary_theme: commute Hamiltonian QAOA for constrained binary optimization
